result.title: ChemExplain: A Multimodal Benchmark for Explanatory Chemical Reasoning
result.summary: Current chemistry benchmarks primarily evaluate outcome prediction or reaction pathway generation, but rarely test whether a model can explain why an observed chemical effect occurs. We introduce ChemExplain, a benchmark of 1,180 multiple-choice chemistry questions drawn from 383 peer-reviewed papers. Each question pairs a molecular or reaction image with an observed chemical effect and four candidate explanations, each associated with a different structural feature visible in the image. Answering requires the model to perceive the depicted structure, apply chemical knowledge, and identify which feature most directly explains the effect, a capability we term explanatory attribution. The correct feature-mechanism relation is derived from supporting evidence in the source paper rather than invented by the question-generation LLM. We construct the benchmark automatically with a multi-agent framework that applies progressive quality control at three stages and validate it with eight chemistry domain experts. The strongest evaluated model reaches 78.6% accuracy, leaving considerable room for improvement. On a 600-question expert-reviewed subset, reasoning-trace analysis classifies 71.4% of the strongest model's errors as attribution failures. Attribution is also the largest error category for the open-source and chemistry-specific models included in our analysis.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 ChemExplain：一个从 383 篇同行评审论文自动构建的 1,180 题化学多模态基准，每题给出分子或反应图像与观察到的化学效应，要求模型在四个各对应不同可见结构特征的候选解释中选出最能解释该效应的一个，并用多智能体流程加专家校验构建；最强模型准确率 78.6%，专家复核子集上 71.4% 的错误被归为「归因失败」。
AI.relevance_reason: 该基准把「答对」与「是否锁定正确的可见结构特征」分开评估，其归因失败诊断与 LVR 关心的视觉证据筛选、答案是否真正使用图像内容、以及错误来源刻画可能直接相关，可供核查。
